correctness.rationale: For each selected rung, precisely one incident horizontal edge is absent at both endpoints. Every proper nonempty rung-support run therefore pairs consecutively and forces paired horizontal deletions. With r selected cuts the spanning 2-factor has exactly r components, so only one cut yields a Hamiltonian cycle. Empty and full rung supports are classified separately with a parity analysis. Every 2-edge Hamiltonian switch is an alternating four-cycle, and for n>=5 all four-cycles are rung squares; this exhausts the moves. Independent direct matching and depth-first-search enumeration, including all pairwise symmetric-difference tests, passed for n=4..18 and n=4..13 respectively. The infinite claim rests on the proof, not on finite tests.

originality.rationale: The finding is the exact graph of Hamiltonian two-edge switches, not a static Hamiltonian-cycle count, cycle-space-span statement, or general reconfiguration complexity theorem. The full-text Heinig 2011 theorem and Lemma 17 address the cycle-space rank of Hamiltonian circuits in prism and Möbius graphs without implying one-switch adjacency. Takaoka 2018 defines the switch and studies other graph classes without this pair of exact decompositions. The known static count in McSorley 1998 is credited. Research-record and topical literature searches found no equivalent switch-graph description. The inaccessible full 1998 paper is explicitly named as a remaining originality risk.
residual_risks: The 1998 McSorley article has no accessible complete text, so an already-published statement about Hamiltonian switches hidden there is not ruled out.
Unindexed older accounts of 2-opt on cubic ladders might establish the same star/discrete dichotomy.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by the ability to locally rearrange Hamiltonian tours under the usual two-edge switch. Two natural cubic families have identical local ladder squares yet radically different exact reconfiguration graphs solely because one seam is twisted: all configurations are frozen on the cylinder, whereas n states become adjacent to one central state on the Möbius strip, with two additional frozen states in odd widths. This natural complete infinite-family mobility classification is not the known Hamiltonian-cycle count and has direct implications for irreducibility of any single-switch Hamiltonian-cycle sampler.
